newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian policeman killed, protests to continue.
newsitem.headline: Albanian policeman killed, protests to continue.

text.p: An Albanian policeman has been shot dead, raising tensions further in this Adriatic port town where three people died in anti-government demonstrations early this week.
The policeman, identified as Shezai Zani, 30, was killed by automatic gunfire on Wednesday near his home in a Vlore suburb, an Interior Ministry statement said.
Vlore police chief Ethem Kurti said Zani was in charge of guarding "places of special importance" and had not taken part in the clashes this week.
"We don't know the motive for his killing," he said.
An anti-government protester was shot dead and two others died of heart attacks during clashes in Vlore this week. About 150 people were injured.
Albania has been rocked by anti-government protests and clashes over the past month after get-rich-quick investment schemes collapsed.
Irate investors in Europe's poorest state, which emerged from 40 years of isolation and Stalinism in 1990, blamed the right-wing government of President Sali Berisha.

They accuse the Berisha government of letting the dubious schemes flourish. Opposition parties have said his Democratic Party used money from the schemes to finance a winning election campaign last year.
Albanians, many of whom pumped their life savings into the double-your-money schemes, plan more anti-government protests on Thursday to demand reimbursement and the resignation of the government.
Art students in Tirana, capital of the Balkan country of 3.4 million people, said they would put on colourful costumes and carry signs appealing for non-violence.
Riot police have moved swiftly in Tirana in recent days to stop any signs of protest and to break up even small gatherings of people.
In Vlore, thousands of protesters vowed to return to the town's central square for a ninth day on Thursday. They marched peacefully shortly before the policeman was killed.

"Here again tomorrow. Here again tomorrow," some 5,000 protesters chanted. After the clashes this week, police were forced to abandon Vlore, where Albania declared independence from Ottoman Turkish rule 1912.
The angry investors cheered opposition leaders who came to Vlore and said they had teamed up with trade unions to form a cross-party political alliance to try to topple the government.
"The government should resign because it is responsible for the biggest-ever theft from the Albanian people," the group said in a declaration.
Vlore has been the scene of some of the worst unrest in Albania since communism fell in 1990.
Protests were sparked by the collapse of a local pyramid investment scheme in which large parts of the population had sunk their life savings, leaving them destitute.

Truckloads of riot police prevented opposition parties from staging a rally in Tirana, some 150 km (90 miles) to the north, in a repeat of last weekend's events when police broke up an anti-government gathering in capital's main Skanderbeg Square.
International criticism of the government's handling of the crisis intensified with the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe saying it was deeply worried about the violence.
Britain said it was appalled by the violence, expressing concern about reports of arrests and intimidation of opposition leaders.
Democratic Party chief and Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu, after a day-long meeting of senior party officials, again blamed the violence on "terrorist acts created by leftist extremists".
Asked earlier whether any cabinet changes were planned, he told Reuters: "Absolutely not."
